issues.legal_issue: A person challenging an official determination about a religious institution through the statutory suit process need not join members of the public under the representative-suit procedure.
material_facts: The institution’s manager claimed that the temple and its endowments were private and had not been dedicated to the public.
The Commissioner determined that the temple was a public excepted temple and appointed members of the manager’s family as hereditary trustees.
The manager challenged the Commissioner’s determination in a suit, naming the Commissioner but not members of the public.
The governing process did not require the Commissioner to give the public notice or a hearing before making the determination, and the rules did not impose such a requirement.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not one requiring the representative-suit procedure, and the public were not necessary parties. The High Court’s contrary judgments were set aside and the appeals were remanded for decision according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 64(2) of the Orissa Hindu Religious Endowment Act, an affected person may sue to modify or set aside the Commissioner’s determination; that provision does not require the public to be joined or the procedure in Order 1, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure to be followed. The statutory scheme makes the Commissioner the representative of the public interest, while individual members of the public lack standing in the relevant proceedings. Section 54(2), which excludes Order 1, rule 8 for suits concerning the administration or management of religious endowments, supports that legislative approach. The judgment also refers by analogy to A.G. v. Brown and Eyre v. Countess of Shaftsbury, concerning the Attorney General’s role in protecting charitable trusts, and rejects the contrary view followed by the High Court in Padma Charan v. Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Orissa.

predicates.statutory_challenge_to_official_classifi: An affected person challenged an official classification of a religious institution through a statutory suit process.
predicates.public_interest_represented_by_responsib: The governing scheme assigned a responsible official the role of representing the public interest in proceedings concerning the religious trust.
predicates.members_of_public_lack_independent_stand: Individual members of the public were not entitled to bring or participate in the relevant proceedings on behalf of the religious trust.
predicates.no_public_participation_required_before_: The process for the official’s initial decision did not require the official to notify or hear members of the public.

issues.definition: When an affected person challenges an official classification through a statutory suit process, the public interest is represented by the responsible official, individual public members lack independent standing, and the initial decision process does not require public participation, the public members need not be joined under the representative-suit procedure.
